rejected.source: <cr>On the 22nd of June 1941, the invasion of the Soviet Union began, opening up the Eastern Front and committing Germany to a two front war. The Axis Powers offensive, invading along a 2,900-kilometer front that stretched from the Arctic Ocean in the North to the Black Sea in the South, saw the greatest invasion force ever known to mankind: around 3.8 million men, supported by around 600,000 vehicles and 600,000 horses.<cr>At the start of the invasion, 80% of the available Soviet military forces in the West had been deployed on the border that faced Axis territories as the first strategic echelon. Its capabilities were greatly reduced from the Purges of the 1930s, strongly affecting the quality of the officer corps. Moreover the standing and morale of the Red Army had been shaken as a result of the Winter War with Finland. On the other hand, after the successful campaigns that had brought Europe to its knees, the German Wehrmacht had consolidated itself as an experienced army, with good training, organisation, and an excellent officer corps.<cr> The titanic struggle between the two major powers and their conflicting ideologies has just begun and it will only end when one of them has been completely destroyed.

The name of these raids comes from a comment made at the time by a spokesman for the German Foreign Office:<cr>'We shall go out and bomb every building in Britain marked with three stars in the Baedeker Guide'<cr>The attempt is an abject failure. Golubev. It was encircled by German forces in June 1941 and largely destroyed.<cr>By late June, the German Army Group Centre surrounded the 3rd, 4th and the 10th Armies in the Battle of Bia?ystok-Minsk. In the end, all the formations and units of the 10th Army were defeated. On 30 June, while trying to cross the highway Minsk-Baranovichi, the army headquarters was destroyed, coming out of the remnants of the environment were addressed by fitting of the 4th Army. The headquarters was officially disbanded on 5 July 1941. The commander of the 10th Army, Major General KD Golubev, and the army artillery commander, Major General M. Barsukov, escaping from the encirclement in a consolidated group with the August 86th Border Detachment of the NKVD, in late July Golubev was appointed commander of 13th Army, which participated in the Battle of Smolensk.<cr>It was formed three times in 1941, next in October in the Southern Front, but its formation 'was halted due to severe battle conditions'.<cr>It was then reformed in November 1941 in the Volga region, with nine divisions, seven of which were new formations. Soviet official websites give the nine divisions as the 322nd, 323rd, 324th, 325th, 326th, 328th and 330th Rifle, and 57th & 75th Cavalry, thus including two cavalry divisions. Nine of these divisions had been formed in the space of three weeks from the reserve of the Moscow Military District and been trained for 12 hours a day. General Lieutenant Filipp Golikov took command. Golikov's 1967 book describes how the army finished its concentration in the Penza area on 8 November 1941, after which 15 days were devoted to combat training and 5 days to construction of living quarters and other facilities. The 172nd Soviet Rifle Division was formed in 1939 and was assigned to the 61st Rifle Corps, 20th Army, Stavka Reserves, located near Tula.

At the start of the war, the 172nd Rifle Division Division was close to 75% strength, but was lacking in support services and transport for heavy equipment. In early July 1941 the Division was rushed forward to take up defensive positions on the Dnieper, near Mogilev, and by 25th of July had been surrounded and completely destroyed. The Divisional Commander, M T Romanov, was wounded trying to break out of the encirclement.

The Division was reformed for a second time in October 1941, based on the 3rd Crimean Motorised Militia Division, and assigned to the 51st Army, then the Coastal Army, and destroyed at Sevastopol in July 1942.

The Division was reformed for a third time in October 1942, in Moscow, and fought at Pavlograd, Kursk, and Kielce. Ended the war with the 102nd Rifle Corps, 13th Army, 1st Ukrainian Front in May 1945.

The Division was awarded the Order of the Red Banner and the Order of Suvorov (2nd Class).

The Soviet 193rd Rifle Division was established in the Kharkov Military District on March 14, 1941. By June 22, 1941 it was still forming near Kamenka in the Kiev Military District and was at close to 50% strength. The Division fought at Rozhits and Kivertsy and by July 8th it was down to 3,500 men. It was destroyed in the Kiev pocket. 

It's Commander, Col. A.K. Berestov, escaped the pocket, and went on to command the 124th Rifle Division, until his death in July 1942.

The division was reformed at Sorochinsk, in the South Urals Military District, in early 1942 and was held in reserve until committed at Stalingrad in September 1942, where it suffered very heavy casualties. In November, 1942 the Division was withdrawn from the field to be rebuilt. 

The rebuilt division was assigned to the 65th Army in February 1943; it was under the command of Lieutenant General Pavel Batov, part of Colonel General K. K. Rokossovski's Central Front. The 193rd would remain under these commanders for the duration of the war.

The Division fought at Kursk, in Operation Bagration, participated in the liberation of Danzig, and finished the war on the Oder river.

The Division was awarded the honorific of Dnepr, Red Banner, Order of Lenin, Order of Suvorov, and Order of Kutuzov.



Nigel Askey, Operation Barbarossa, Vol IIIA 

Steen Ammentrop, The Generals.

rejected.source: The 19th Hungarian Infantry Brigade was formed in 1939. Its TOE consisted of 9,500 men under a major-general with 2 infantry regiments (each with 3 battalions and a machine gun company), an artillery regiment with 7 batteries and various support troops. In January 1942 the Germans demanded more Hungarian forces for the Eastern Front and most Hungarian infantry brigades were reclassified as 'light divisions'. Their TOE however remained largely unchanged. The brigade was renamed the 19th Light Division. The Hungarian Government reluctantly agreed to support the Germans 1942 summer offensive Fall Blau and allocated the Hungarian Second Army to the task. Each light division in the Second Army was reinforced with three battalions from sister divisions in Hungary but nonetheless each division was only slightly larger than half the size of its German counterparts. Second Army's role in the offensive was to guard the German northern flank on the Don River. During the Stalingrad Campaign the Second Army suffered over 60% casualties but was generally able to retreat in good order. By 1943 the division was part of the Hungarian Occupation Group assigned to security duties in occupied Russia. As part of a general reorganization of the Hungarian Army after Stalingrad the 19th Light Division was merged with other units and renamed the 19th Reserve Division. In January of 1944 the Hungarian First Army to which the division was subordinate, mobilized to defend Hungary's northern Carpathian frontier against the advancing Red Army. The division was disbanded in August 1944.<cr><cr>Dr. Nigel Thomas and Lazlo Pal Szabo, The Royal Hungarian Army in World War II<cr><cr>Entry courtesy Chris Munson

On 22 June 1941 the 1st Moscow Motor Rifle Division was part of the 7th Mechanised Corps, alongside the 14th and 18th tank divisions in the Moscow Military District, assigned to the 20th Army.
23 June 1941, the 1st Moscow Motor Rifle Division was replenished to the full strength of 10831 men. It was the first Soviet formation to use T-34 tanks, at Borisov, on June 30, 1941.
11 July 1941, after suffering heavy losses, the 1st Moscow Motor Rifle Division was moved to the reserve of 20th army and placed north of Orsha, and was completely encircled by the German forces 14 July 1941.
25 July 1941, the elements of 6th and 175th motor rifle regiments of 1st Moscow Motor Rifle Division break encirclement near Mogilev, but have suffered more losses in the heavy rearguard fighting by 30 July 1941. During that period, heavy personnel flow left few if any of the initial combatants.
By 5 August 1941, remnants of the 1st Moscow Motor Rifle Division were wiped out after being encircled again in Smolensk region, in unclear circumstances.
5 August 1941, the 1st Moscow Motor Rifle Division was re-formed anew within 20th army, 18 August 1941 renamed 1st armoured division and on September 21, 1941, it was renamed the 1st Guards Moscow Motor Rifle Division. The division was renamed (again) as the 1st Guards Rifle Division, in January 1943.
30 August 1941, the 1st armoured division was participating in the Yelnya Offensive, forcing back 28th Jager Division. Due heavy losses, the division was stopped advancing 10 September 1941 and was withdrawn to behind of Vop River.
18 September 1941, the 1st armoured division was withdrawn to Mozhaysk for replenishment and subordinated directly to Stavka.
30 September 1941, the 1st Guards Moscow Motor Rifle Division was assigned to 40th army and sent to Sumy region. After initial advances, the 1st Guards Moscow Motor Rifle Division started to retreat 6 October 1941 as First Battle of Kharkov was being lost by Soviet forces. After losing Sumy 10 October 1941, the division was withdrawn to the reserve and sent back to Moscow.
21 October 1941, the division was assigned to 3rd army and arrived to Naro-Fominsk. The 1st Guards Moscow Motor Rifle Division lost 70% of personnel in urban warfare before retreating from Naro-Fominsk 25 October 1941. Attempt to re-take Naro-Fominsk 28 October 1941 have failed. The division remained in Naro-Fominsk area until end of November 1941.
29 January 1942, the division liberated the village of Myatlevo in cooperation with the 415th Rifle Division during the winter counteroffensive in front of Moscow.
In 1942, the 1st Guards Moscow Motor Rifle Division was participating in Battle of Rzhev.
In July 1943, the 1st Guards Rifle Division was participating in Operation Kutuzov, in October 1943 - in Bryansk offensive, and in December 1943 - in Haradok offensive.
In JanuaryJuly 1944, the 1st Guards Rifle Division was advancing in Vitebsk - Minsk direction with heavy fighting, and was awarded 'Minsk' honorific 13 July 1944.
In November 1944, the division invaded East Prussia in Gusev area, and finally stormed Knigsberg in April 1945.
21-26 April 1945, the 1st Guards Rifle Division ended the war by storming Baltiysk as part of 11th Guards Army of the 3rd Belorussian Front.<cr><cr>

The 1st Mechanized Division was formed from the 1st Rifle Division in May 1940 in Moscow Military District.<cr>
The 1st was one of the earliest Mechanized Divisions formed, and even though it was assigned to 7th Mechanized Corps, it retained some of the personality of the 1st 'Moscow Proletariat' Rifle Division, which had been a Parade or showpiece unit permanently stationed in Moscow.<cr>
By 22 June 1941 the 1st Mechanized was actually stationed just outside of Moscow in Vyazma, with 12,000 men (actually overstrength in authorized personnel), 100% of authorized artillery and heavy weapons, and 225 BT-7M tanks in the tank regiment - the newest and most modern 'light tanks' available in quantity.<cr>
Before the rest of 7th Mechanized Corps, 1st Mechanized Division was alerted to move to the front on the morning of 22 June. On the way forward through Orsha (west of Smolensk) the division added 10 KVs and 30 T-34s from Tank Training units in Western Military District. When the division went into battle for the first time 26 - 30 June, it also had under command a battalion of students from the Borisov Tank-Technical School. Because of these additions, the Germans mistakenly thought that this division had been authorized a special complement of heavy and medium tanks not found in other mechanized divisions. To add to the confusion, German intelligence variously identified the unit as the 'Moscow' division, the 'Stalin Guards' division, or the 'Moscow Guards' division.<cr>
For a time in August 1941, both the Germans and the Red Army (unofficially)identified it as the 1st Tank Division - chiefly because it still had a functioning tank regiment after almost all the other tank and mechanized divisions in Western Front had been destroyed.<cr>7th Mechanized Corps staff was used to form a new headquarters for 16th Army near Smolensk in early July, so 1st Mechanized Division became an independant 'fire brigade' unit for Western Front, fighting frequently under either 16th or 20th Army command east of Smolensk throughout July and August, 1941. Its division commander, Col A. I. Lizyukov, was one of the first wartime recipients of the Hero of the Soviet Union medal - the Soviet equivalent of the Medal of Honor or Victoria Cross.<cr>
By 15 September, 1st Mechanized Division was in Western Front reserveswith 45 tanks total and 600 riflemen left in each motorized rifle regiment. In recognition of the division's combat record - in persistant survivability, if not strategic success - on 21 September 1941 1st Mechanized Division became the 1st Guards Motorized Division.<cr><cr>Soviet Order of Battle Volume I by Charles C. Sharp

The 201st Rifle Division was formed as an Red Army national unit during August 1941 in Gorki, Moscow Military District from the remains of the 24th Territorial Rifle Corps, and assigned to the 33rd Army.<cr>
It was originally designated as the 201st Latvian Rifle Division, as the basis of the division was the 76th Independent Latvian Rifle Regiment. By December 1941 the division had 10,348 personnel, of whom 51% were ethnic Latvians, 26% ethnic Russians, 17% Jews and 6% others.<cr> 
The first combat the division experienced was during the counter-offensive at Moscow in the areas of Naro-Fominsk and Borovsk where it suffered 55% casualties. It also fought in the battle for Staraya Russa (from 16 February 1942 until 4 April), and for the Demyansk bridgehead. By June 1942 only 36% of the division were Latvian-speaking, and a year later this figure was reduced to 32%.<cr> 
The division was renamed as the 43rd Guards Rifle Division in October 1942 and was known as the Latvian Guards.<cr>
A new 201st Rifle Division was raised from the 27th Rifle Brigade at Shlisselburg, near Leningrad, in November 1943, assigned to the 23rd Army. It served in the Leningrad and Baltic coast areas.

The 202nd Mechanized Division had almost all of its assigned artillery and heavy weapons on 22 June 1941, but only about 200 light T-26 tanks, and less than a third of the trucks and tractors required to move its men and equipment. The biggest problem for the division, however, was that it had only 50% of its authorized radios, the divisional signal battalion was short 2/3 of its assigned technicians, and when the Germans attacked the division's elements were scattered over 60 km apart! When 12th Mechanized Corps went into battle, the division simply could not organize itself fast enough to join the tank divisions. As a result, the 125th Tank Regiment was taken from the division and added to 28th Tank Division on 26 June, to try to make up for tank losses in that unit.<cr>
In late July 202nd Mech, which was now effectively only a 'semi motorized' rifle division, was assigned directly to llth Army. At the start of the war the 218th Mechanised Division was assigned to the 18th Mechanised Corps, 9th Army, Southern Front, and was close to 80% establishment, though lacking in tanks and armoured cars. In early September, 1941, this mechanised division was renamed as the 218th Rifle Division, withdrawn to the reserves of the Southern Front, and ended 1941 assigned to the 12th Army.

The division was deactivated in July 1942 and was formed for a second time in mid 1943 where it assisted in the recapture of Kiev and Zhitomir, for which it was awarded the Order of the Red Banner. At this time the divisional commander, S.F. Skliarov, was killed in an air raid.

At the end of the war it was assigned to the 6th Army, 1st Ukrainian Front.

The 25th Tank Corps was formed in June 1942 in the Moscow Military District.<cr>The 25th Tank Corps moved to Bryansk Front area at Voronezh in late June and then, on 5 July, was assigned to 5th Tank Army. The 25th was roughly handled in the tank battles around Voronezh, but not caught up in the German advance to the Don and the Volga Rivers. Instead, 25th Tank Corps remained in the Voronezh area until December, when it was shifted south and took part in the 'Malyy Saturn' Operation with 1st Guards Army. By January 1943 the 25th Tank Corps was part of Southwestern Front's Mobile Group with additional supporting units.<cr>Unfortunately, between the continuous advances and fighting from December to February and Manstein's counterattack in late February and March 1943, 25th Tank Corps suffered almost 90% losses and in March 1943, went into STAVKA Reserves to be rebuilt and refitted. In July, the corps went back into action with 11th Guards Army in the Bryansk Front.<cr>The 25th Tank Corps fought only briefly in the summer offensives that started in July-August after Kursk, and by late August was back in reserve in the Moscow Military District. There it remained until October 1943, probably reequipping all the tank brigades with T-34 tanks in 3 tank battalions each. In late October 1943 it was sent to 1st Ukrainian Front, with which it remained for the rest of the war. At that time the corps included additional supporting units.<cr>In the fighting after the liberation of Kiev on the right bank of the Dnepr 25th Tank Corps fought under 13th and 60th Armies west of Kiev. By March 1944 the corps' SU regiments had been changed.<cr>The 25th Tank Corps was part of 1st Cavalry Mechanized Group for the
Lvov-Sandomir Operation in July 1944. In September 1944 the corps received 296th Guards Light Artillery Regiment (24 76mm guns) At the end of 1944, as the Front prepared for the Vistula-Oder Operation, 25th Tank Corps converted 746th Antitank Battalion into the 746th Heavy SU Regiment (ISU-122s).<cr>As a result of the operations in January 1945 that advanced the corps to the Oder River, the 746th was redesignated as 262nd Guards Heavy SU Regiment. rejected.translation: 第25坦克军于1942年6月在莫斯科军区组建。该部队于6月下旬转移到沃罗涅日的布良斯克方面军区域，并于7月5日被分配给第5坦克集团军。<cr>第25坦克军在沃罗涅日附近的坦克战斗中遭受重创，但没有卷入德国向顿河和伏尔加河推进的攻势。相反，该坦克军一直留在沃罗涅日地区直到12月，并于此时被转移到南方并参加了“小土星行动”，与第1近卫集团军协同作战。<cr>到1943年1月，第25坦克军成为西南方面军机动部队的一部分，并有额外的支援单位。遗憾的是，在从12月至次年2月连续推进和战斗期间以及曼施坦因在1943年2月下旬至3月发起反攻时，该坦克军遭受了近90%的损失，并于1943年3月进入最高统帅部大本营预备队进行重建。<cr>7月，该部队与第11近卫集团军一起在布良斯克方面军投入战斗。它仅短暂参与了从7月至8月开始的夏季攻势，在8月下旬又回到了莫斯科军区的预备队中。<cr>直到1943年10月，它可能一直在为每个坦克营配备T-34坦克，并于该月被派往第1乌克兰方面军。此后，该部队一直留在那里直至战争结束，并包括额外的支援单位。<cr>在解放基辅后，在第聂伯河右岸作战期间，第25坦克军隶属于第13集团军和第60集团军，位于基辅以西地区。到1944年3月，该部的SU团已经进行了调整。第25坦克军于1944年7月在利沃夫-桑多尔行动期间隶属于第1机械化骑兵集团。1944年9月，该军接收了第296近卫轻炮兵团（装备有24门76毫米火炮）。到1944年底，随着方面军为维斯瓦河-奥得河行动做准备，第25坦克军将第746反坦克营改编为第746重型自行火炮团（ISU-122）。<cr>由于1945年1月的作战行动推进该军到达奥德河畔，第746团被重新指定为第262近卫重型自行火炮团。这是战争期间该军组织上的最后一次变更。第25坦克军于1945年5月在柏林附近结束战争，在第一次梯队中参与了第一乌克兰方面军的柏林行动。<cr>苏联二战战斗序列 第二卷作者：查尔斯·C·夏普

rejected.source: The 27th Rifle Division was formed in November 1918 during the Russian Civil War. It later fought in the war with Poland shortly after World War I and suffered heavy losses. The division returned to Poland in 1939 and took part in the joint Nazi and Soviet Invasion of Poland as part of the 3rd Army's 4th Rifle Corps.<cr>At the start of Operation Barbarossa on 22 June 1941, the division was again part of 4th Rifle Corps in the Western Special Military District which quickly became the Western Front. The division was attacked by the German 162nd and 256th Infantry Divisions. Its regiments fought separately as they retreated eastwards towards Sok?ka. By June 24th the division had lost 40% of its personnel and the following day unsuccessfully tried to defend the Swis?ocz river line. In accordance with orders, it defended the line until the end of the day when it was annihilated. Only small groups of soldiers from the division survived to reach Soviet lines in July and early August. The division was officially disbanded on September 19, 1941.<cr>The division was reformed in August 1941 at Arkhangelsk and renamed the Rebolsky Direction Division in September 1941. The division subsequently fought against the Finnish Army. The division was subordinated to the 26th Army of the Karelian Front in May 1942 and was deployed in the far north of Russia until the end of 1944. The unit completed the war with the 19th Army of the 2nd Belorussian Front in May 1945.<cr><cr><cr><cr>Entry courtesy Chris Munson
rejected.translation: 第27步兵师成立于1918年11月的俄国内战期间。该师后来参加了第一次世界大战后不久与波兰的战争，并遭受了重大损失。该师于1939年返回波兰，作为西部特别军区第三集团军第四步兵军的一部分参与了纳粹德国和苏联对波兰的联合入侵。<cr>巴巴罗萨行动开始时（1941年6月22日），该师再次隶属于西部方面军辖区内的第四步兵军。德军第162步兵师和第256步兵师对该师进行了攻击。其团级单位在撤退至索科尔卡的过程中各自为战。<cr>到6月24日，该师已损失了40%的人员，并于次日试图防守斯维斯洛奇河防线未果。根据命令，该师一直坚守到当天结束时被彻底摧毁。只有少数士兵在7月和8月初到达苏军阵地幸存下来。<cr>该师于1941年9月19日正式解散。<cr>1941年8月，该师在阿尔汉格尔斯克重建，并于同年9月更名为雷博尔斯基方向师。该师随后与芬兰军队作战。该师于1942年5月隶属于卡累利阿方面军的第26集团军，在俄罗斯北部地区一直战斗到1944年底。<cr>该单位在1945年5月作为第二白俄罗斯方面军第19集团军的一部分完成了战争。<cr><cr>克里斯·芒森提供

The 29th Tank Corps was formed February 1943 in Moscow Military District as part of STAVKA Reserves.The 29th Tank Corps was immediately (15 March 1943) assigned to 5th Guards Tank Army, which was being reformed after the winter battles. The corps remained under 5th Guards Tank Army until May 1945. By 1 July 1943 the tank army was in Steppe Front behind the Kursk salient.<cr>On the morning of 12 July, in the 'biggest tank battle of the war' at Prokhorovka, 29th Tank Corps was right in the middle of 5th Guards Tank Army's attacking line. The corps lost 60% of its tanks on that day and the next, and spent the last two weeks of July repairing and average of 20 tanks a day to
rebuild the tank brigades. 29th Tank Corps fought in the Battle of Kharkov and the advance to the Dnepr River throughout August-December 1943. In September 1943 1549th Heavy SU Regiment (SU-152s) was added to the corps, and in October 1943 the corps finally received its rocket unit: 11th Guards Mortar Battalion (8 BM-13 launchers) . 38th Armored Car Battalion was removed after the Kursk Battle, and the 1446th SU Regiment re-equipped with SU-85s sometime in late 1943. Also during the continuous reinforcement of the corps to try to cover the casualties, all the tank brigades were completely re-equipped with T-34 tanks in 3 tank battalions of 65 tanks by the end of 1943.<cr>29th Tank Corps also received recognition for its performance in combat. On 10 December 1943 the corps received the honorific title 'Znamenskikh' for liberating Znamensk, and on 8 January 1944 the corps received the Order of the Red Banner for its performance in the Kirovograd Operation. In February, for its exploits during the Korsun-Shevchenkovskii ('Korsun Pocket') Operation, the 1549th Heavy SU Regiment became the 339th Guards Heavy SU Regiment, and then was removed from the corps so it could be sent into reserve and re-equipped. In May 1944 29th Tank Corps and 5th Guards Tank Army finally went into reserve after 9 months of almost continuous combat.<cr>The 29th Tank Corps was committed in the drive into the southern Baltic states in July 1944, and fought in that region for the rest of 1944. In addition to its assigned units, the corps frequently controlled or was directly supported by units from 5th Guards Tank Army and other units.In October 1944, 165th was redesignated as a Light Artillery Regiment (still with 24 76mm guns) and assigned to 29th Tank Corps permanently. When the Soviet offensives started in January 1945, 29th Tank Corps had been built up.<cr>On 14 January 1945, when the corps went over to the offensive, it had 149 tanks and 111 SUs on hand - which meant that the tank brigades were slightly under strength (averaging 50 tanks each out of 65 authorized) but the 4 SU regiments in the corps were almost 1/3 over strength! 29th Tank Corps ended the war in May 1945 in East Prussia, still part of 5th Guards Tank Army.<cr><cr>Soviet Order of Battle World War II Volume II by Charles C. Sharp
rejected.translation: 第29坦克军于1943年2月在莫斯科军区组建，作为最高统帅部大本营的预备部队。该坦克军于1943年3月15日立即被分配给正在重组的第5近卫坦克集团军，后者是在冬季战斗后进行重建。直到1945年5月，该军一直隶属于第5近卫坦克集团军。<cr>截至1943年7月1日，坦克集团军位于斯捷普方面军，在库尔斯克突出部的后面。<cr>在7月12日上午进行的“战争中最大的坦克战斗”——普罗霍罗夫卡战役中，第29坦克军处于第5近卫坦克集团军攻击线的中心位置。<cr>该军在这两天内损失了60%的坦克，并且在接下来的两周里每天平均修复20辆坦克以重建坦克旅。<cr>1943年8月至12月，第29坦克军参加了哈尔科夫战役和向第聂伯河推进的战斗。<cr>1943年9月，重型SU-152自行火炮团（1549团）加入该军。同年10月，该军终于收到了火箭部队：第11近卫迫击炮营（8门BM-13发射器）。<cr>库尔斯克战役后，装甲车团第38团被移除。<cr>1446团自行火炮也于1943年底某个时候重新装备了SU-85。在持续增援该军以弥补伤亡的过程中，所有坦克旅都完全换装为T-34坦克，在三个坦克营中每营有65辆坦克，到1943年底为止。<cr>第29坦克军也在战斗中获得了认可。1943年12月10日，该军因解放扎缅斯克而获得“扎缅斯克”荣誉称谓；1944年1月8日，该军又因为在基洛夫格勒行动中的表现被授予红旗勋章。2月份，在科尔孙-舍甫琴科夫斯基（“科尔孙包围圈”）行动中，第1549重型SU团成为第339近卫重型SU团，并随后从军中调出进入预备队并重新装备。1944年5月，第29坦克军和第5近卫坦克集团军在连续作战9个月后终于转入预备队。<cr>1944年7月，该军被投入到向波罗的海南部诸州的进攻中，并于同年余下的时间里一直在该地区作战。除了其编配单位外，该军还经常控制或直接得到第5近卫坦克集团军和其他部队的支持。<cr>1944年10月，第165团被改编为轻型炮兵团（仍配备24门76毫米火炮），并永久分配给第29坦克军。当苏联攻势于1945年1月开始时，第29坦克军已经得到了加强。<cr>1945年1月14日，该军转入进攻时拥有149辆坦克和111辆SU——这意味着坦克旅的编制略低于满编（平均每个旅有50辆坦克，而授权编制为65辆），但军中的4个SU团则几乎超编三分之一！第29坦克军在1945年5月结束战争时仍属于第5近卫坦克集团军。

32nd Antiaircraft Battalion<cr><cr>The 32nd Tank Division was one of the best-equipped units formed in 1941, and one of the best-equipped tank divisions in the Red Army in June 1941. KVs and T-34 tanks. In addition, the division had only 50.3% of the officers and 42.9% of NCOs assigned, so that experienced leadership was lacking as well as time to train. 然而，在6月和7月的乌克兰西部坦克战中，第32坦克师还是设法坚持下来了。1941年8月，第4机械化军司令部解散，第32坦克师撤至预备队，并在那里被解散，人员用于组建第8坦克旅。

In fact the 3rd Army command did not have any operative attributes until 2 July 1941, when the ground offensive started also in the Romanian sector.<cr>In 1942 in the Caucasus, the 3rd Army initially consisted of the Cavalry Corps (Romania) (5th, 6th and 9th Cavalry Divisions) and the 1st Army Corps (Romania) (2nd Mountain Division and German 298th Infantry Division). 3rd Army was subordinated to the German 17th Army. It also had 3 observation squadrons assigned to it. However, after reorganization, on 7 August, only the Cavalry Corps remained with it.<cr>Along with the Romanian 4th Army, the Third Army bore the brunt of the Soviet Operaton Uranus, which saw the German Sixth Army encircled and destroyed during the Battle of Stalingrad.<cr>The Romanian Third Army, commanded by General Petre Dumistrescu, was transferred from the Caucasus and replaced five Italian and two German divisions between Blij Perekopa and Bokovkaya, with the task of defending a front 138 km long, far beyond its capabilities. To make things worse, the Soviets had two bridgeheads over the Don River, at Serafimovich and Kletskaya, which the German High Command ignored, despite repeated requests by General Dumitrescu for permission to eliminate them. At the start of the Soviet offensive in November 1942, the Third Army had a nominal strength of 152,492 Romanian troops and 11,211 German troops, being made up from 1st, 2nd, 4th and 5th Corps in a single echelon (1st Cavalry, 5th, 6th, 7th, 9th, 11th, 13th and 14th Infantry Divisions) from West to East, with 7th Cavalry and 15th Infantry Divisions in reserve. The Long Range Recon (Do-17M) and the 112th Liaison Squadrons (Fleet 10G) were also at its disposal. In November came the German XLVIII Panzer Corps, composed of the 22nd Panzer Division and the 1st Romanian Armored Division, which also was put in reserve. It also had the 2nd, 4th, 5th and 8th Motorized Heavy Artillery Regiments and the 41st Independent Motorized Heavy Artillery Battalion. Opposite the 3rd Army was the Southwestern Front, comprising the 1st Guards Army, 5th Tank Army and the Soviet 21st Army, with a force of 5,888 artillery pieces, 728 tanks and 790 planes.<cr>On 19 November at 0530, in the sector of the Third Romanian Army, a violent artillery barrage battered the entire front line. The weather conditions were harsh: blizzards, snow, -20 degrees Celsius, which made close air support impossible. The Soviets assaulted the positions of the 14th Infantry Division with the 5th Tank Army and the junction between the 13th Infantry Division and the 1st Cavalry Division with the 21st Army, with a total of 338,631 men against three weak divisions. The 37mm and 47mm AT guns were useless against Soviet T-34 tanks, so the Romanian troops had to use grenades, anti-tank mines and Molotov cocktails. In the first hours, they managed to delay the advance and destroy some tanks, but later they had to retreat or face encirclement. The Soviets also attacked west of Sarisa Valley and at Raspopinskaya, but were repulsed. In response to the situation that developed south of Kletskaya, the German 48th Panzer Corps was ordered to move towards the Soviet main thrust and shortly afterwards, the 22nd Panzer Division was redirected to the northwest towards Bolsoy and, reaching Petshany, it engaged Soviet armor. By evening, the 1st Romanian Armored Division reached Sirkovsky, making preparations to attack Bolsoy the next day.<cr>In the first day of the offensive, the Soviet forces succeeded in making two large breaches in the defences of the Third Romanian Army: one in the center, 1618 km wide and 15 km deep and one in the right wing, between the Third Romanian Army and the German Sixth Army, 1012 km wide and 3540 km deep.<cr>On 20 November, the Soviet armored and motorized forces advanced towards Kalach, with the intention of encircling the 6th Army embroiled in ferocious fighting at Stalingrad. The 22nd Panzer Division, overwhelmed at Petshany by the large number of Soviet tanks, withdrew north to Bol. Donschynka. The Romanian 1st Armored Division, without any available radio contact, tried to advance to Petshany in order to make the junction with the 22nd Panzer Division, but was forced to stop a few kilometers west of Korotovsky by stiff Soviet resistance and numerous counterattacks by Soviet tanks, flowing between the German 22nd and the Romanian 1st, occupying the Varlamovsky and Peralasovsky villages and making the junction with forces coming from Gromsky, thus encircling the 5th Corps. In the 4th Corps' sector, 40 Soviet tanks attacked the 15th Infantry Division but were repulsed by evening with heavy loses. Meanwhile, the 7th Cavalry Division unsuccessfully tried to block the enemy's advance; the right wing of the division, which had fully received the blow, retreated south while the left wing was reassigned to the 9th Infantry Division. Also, the 1st Cavalry Division had to retreat towards Stalingrad and was subordinated to the 6th Army. At the end of the day, the defence position of the Third Romanian Army had a 70 km wide gap in the centre. In this pocket were encircled the 1st Armored Division, three infantry divisions (5th, 6th and 15th) and remains of other two infantry divisions (13th and 14th). The former commander of the 6th Infantry Division, Major General Mihail Lascar, took command of the troops from the infantry divisions and formed the 'General Lascar' Group (40,000 men). At this point, the command point of the Third Army began moving to Morozovskaya.<cr>On 21 November, the 22nd Panzer Division tried to advance towards Perelasovsky in order to make the junction with the 1st Armored Division and to relieve the 'General Lascar' Group, but failed and was stopped the next day between Bol. Donschynka and Perelasovky. The 1st Romanian Armored Division advanced towards Bol. Donschynka, where it was hoping to find the German division, but the village was under Soviet control and then headed south and, after grim fighting, crossed the Chir River on the 25 November.<cr>On 22 November, the encircled 'General Lascar' Group, which had been ordered to resist at any cost, was attacked and transmitted its last message. They had run out of food and each gun had only 40 rounds left and after refusing the Soviet proposal to surrender they were entirely destroyed. Only the 1st Battalion of the 15 Infantry Regiment (6th infantry Division), commanded by Major Gheorghe Rasconescu, succeeded in getting to the Chir River with all its soldiers and equipment. His battalion had managed to prevent the Soviet 8th Cavalry Division from capturing the vital German airfield at Oblivkaya from 26 November to 3 December.<cr>On 23 November, the Soviet troops of the South-Western Front and of the Stalingrad Front met at Kalach-na-Donu, completing the encirclement of the German 6th Army, parts of the Romanian 4th Army and six other Romanian infantry divisions as well as one cavalry division.<cr><cr>

1941年6月22日，第3集团军包括第4军（第6步兵师和第7步兵师）、骑兵军（第5骑兵旅和第8骑兵旅）、山地军（第1、第2和第4山地旅）以及两个独立炮兵团和一个目标搜索炮兵连。<cr>在北方的“慕尼黑”行动中，第3集团军仅保留了山地军（第1、第2和第4山地旅，第8骑兵旅和第7步兵师），因为骑兵军（第5和第6骑兵旅）直接隶属于德国第11集团军。实际上直到1941年7月2日地面进攻开始时，第3集团军指挥部才具备实际作战能力。<cr>在1942年的高加索地区，第3集团军最初包括罗马尼亚骑兵军（第5、第6和第9骑兵师）以及罗马尼亚第1军（第2山地师和德国第298步兵师）。第3集团军隶属于德国第17集团军。它还拥有3个侦察中队。然而，重组后，在8月7日，只有骑兵军留在其编制内。<cr>与罗马尼亚第4集团军一起，第3集团军在苏联的“天王星行动”中遭受重创，该行动导致德国第6集团军在斯大林格勒战役中被包围并消灭。<cr>罗马尼亚第三集团军，由彼得鲁·杜米特雷斯库将军指挥，从高加索地区调来，取代了布利佩雷科帕至博科夫卡亚之间五个意大利师和两个德国师的防区。该集团军的任务是防守长达138公里的防线，远远超出了其能力范围。更糟糕的是，苏联在顿河上拥有塞拉芬维奇和克列茨卡亚两处桥头堡，而德军最高指挥部无视了杜米特雷斯库将军多次请求批准清除这些据点的要求。

1942年11月苏军攻势开始时，第三集团军名义上有152,492名罗马尼亚士兵和11,211名德国士兵。该集团军由第一、第二、第四和第五军组成，在一个梯队中（从西到东依次为：第一骑兵师、第五步兵师、第六步兵师、第七步兵师、第九步兵师、第十一步兵师、第十三步兵师、第十四步兵师），第七骑兵师和第十五步兵师处于预备状态。该集团军还拥有远程侦察（Do-17M）中队和联络机（Fleet 10G）中队。

11月，德国XLVIII装甲军加入，由第二十二装甲师和第一罗马尼亚装甲师组成，并被置于预备状态。此外还有第二、第四、第五和第八摩托化重型炮兵团以及独立的第四十一摩托化重型炮兵团。

面对第三集团军的是西南方面军，包括近卫第一集团军、坦克第五集团军和苏联第21集团军，拥有5,888门火炮、728辆坦克和790架飞机。<cr>11月19日凌晨5点30分，在第三罗马尼亚集团军的防区内，猛烈的炮火轰击了整个前线。天气恶劣：暴风雪、积雪和零下20摄氏度的低温使得近距离空中支援变得不可能。苏联军队用第5坦克集团军攻击了第14步兵师的位置，并用第21集团军攻击了第13步兵师与第1骑兵师之间的结合部，总兵力达338,631人，面对三个薄弱的罗马尼亚师。37毫米和47毫米反坦克炮对苏联T-34坦克无能为力，因此罗马尼亚部队不得不使用手榴弹、反坦克地雷和莫洛托夫鸡尾酒进行反击。在最初的几个小时里，他们设法延缓了进攻并摧毁了一些坦克，但后来要么被迫撤退，要么面临被包围的危险。苏联军队还在萨里斯河谷以西和拉斯波平斯卡亚地区发动攻击，但均遭到了击退。为了应对克列茨卡亚南部局势的发展，德军第48装甲军接到命令向苏军主要突击方向移动，并很快将第22装甲师重新部署到西北方向的博洛伊，到达佩什尼后与苏联坦克部队交战。傍晚时分，第1罗马尼亚装甲师抵达西尔科夫斯基，准备第二天进攻博洛伊。

在第一天的攻势中，苏军成功地在第三罗马尼亚集团军防线上制造了两个大的突破口：一个位于中央，宽达16.18公里、纵深15公里；另一个位于右翼，在第三罗马尼亚集团军与德军第6集团军之间，宽达10.12公里、纵深35.4公里。11月20日，苏联装甲和机械化部队向卡拉萨前进，意图包围陷入斯大林格勒激烈战斗中的第6集团军。在佩什阿尼被大量苏军坦克压倒的第22装甲师撤退到博尔·多恩申卡以北。没有无线电联系的罗马尼亚第1装甲师试图推进到佩什阿尼，与第22装甲师会合，但因遭到苏联部队顽强抵抗和来自苏军坦克的多次反攻而被迫在科罗托夫斯基西面几公里处停止前进。苏军坦克流窜于德军第22装甲师和罗马尼亚第1装甲师之间，占领了瓦尔拉莫夫斯克村和佩拉拉斯克村，并与从格罗姆斯基来的部队会合，从而包围了第5军。在第4军的防区，40辆苏军坦克攻击了第15步兵师，但傍晚时分被击退，损失惨重。与此同时，第7骑兵师未能阻止敌人的推进；该师右翼完全遭到打击后撤向南面，左翼则转隶给第9步兵师。此外，第1骑兵师也必须撤往斯大林格勒，并隶属于第6集团军。到当天结束时，第三罗马尼亚集团军的防御阵地在中央形成了70公里宽的缺口，在这个包围圈内被围困的是第1装甲师、三个步兵师（第5、第6和第15）以及另外两个步兵师（第13和第14）的部分残部。原第6步兵师指挥官米哈伊尔·拉扎尔少将接管了来自各步兵师的部队，并组建了“拉扎尔将军”集团（约4万人）。此时，第三集团军指挥部开始向莫罗佐夫斯卡亚转移。<cr>11月21日，第22装甲师试图向佩雷拉索夫斯基推进，以与第1装甲师会合并解救“拉斯卡将军”集团，但未能成功，并于次日在博尔·多恩什因卡和佩雷拉索夫斯基之间被阻止。第1罗马尼亚装甲师则朝博尔·多恩什因卡前进，希望在那里找到德军，但村庄已被苏联控制，随后向南推进，在惨烈的战斗后于11月25日渡过奇尔河。<cr>11月22日，“拉斯卡将军”集团被包围并遭到攻击。该集团奉命不惜一切代价抵抗，并发送了最后一条信息。他们已经断粮，每门炮只剩下40发弹药，在拒绝苏联提出的投降建议后，整个集团被彻底消灭。只有第6步兵师的第15步兵团（第6步兵师）的第一营在乔治·拉松内斯库少校指挥下成功带领所有士兵和装备到达奇尔河。<cr>从11月26日至12月3日，该团阻止了苏联第8骑兵师占领关键的德国机场奥布利夫卡。<cr>11月23日，西南方面军和斯大林格勒方面的苏军在卡拉奇会合，完成了对德军第6集团军、罗马尼亚第4集团军的部分以及另外六个罗马尼亚步兵师和一个骑兵师的包围圈。

The 41st Tank Division was formed March 1941 at Vladimir-Volynsk in Kiev Special Military District as part of 22nd Mechanized Corps. On 22 June 1941 included:<cr>
81st Tank Regiment
82nd Tank Regiment
41st Motorized Rifle Regiment
41st Howitzer Regiment

41st Motorized Pontoon Battalion
41st Antiaircraft Battalion<cr>
The 41st Tank Division, on paper, was well-equipped with armor by 22 June 1941: it had 100% of the authorized number of tanks. The reality was much worse: 342 of the tanks were T-26s, and almost 15% of those were unservicable on 15 June. The 31 KV-II heavy tanks had only arrived in the division a week before the Germans attacked: the crews were untrained on them, and there was not one round of ammunition available for their 152mm guns. While the rifle regiment was almost full strength in personnel, and had all its heavy weapons and machine guns, it was missing most of the trucks to move itself, and the howitzer regiment did not have a single tractor to move its guns. The reconnaissance battalion, antiaircraft battalion, and pontoon battalion were essentially company-sized units, missing 2/3 of their equipment.<cr> To make things, worse, from the first day of the war 41st Tank Division was attached to 15th Rifle Corps HQ, which constantly detached tank companies to support the rifle units. Most of these companies, opposing German panzer units without support and outnumbered at the point of contact, were destroyed before they could rejoin the division. On 26 June no less than 4 out of 8 tank battalions were detached to infantry support. By 6 July, the division had lost most of the T-26s, and had only 9 of the KV-IIs left. By 25 August, the division was down to 2000 men and a handful of tanks and armored cars. In September it was destroyed in the Kiev pocket.<cr><cr>Soviet Order of Battle Volume I by Charles C. Sharp

Alpini mountain infantry were considered elite units in the Italian Army. Each division consisted of two Alpini regiments with three battalions each, one Alpine artillery regiment, one mixed engineer battalion and various support troops for a total divisional strength of over 17,000 men. Each Alpini division also possessed nearly 5,000 mules and 500 vehicles of various types. The division participated in every Italian Campaign in World War II with the exception of the North African Campaign. The division was one of three Alpini sent to fight on the Eastern Front with the Italian 8th Army in the summer of 1942. The division was originally to be deployed to the Caucasus Mountains but instead found itself, along with the rest of the 8th Army, stretched along a 160 mile section of the Don River between the Hungarian Second Army and Romanian 3rd Army on the German left flank at the start of Operation Little Saturn. The division, along with most of the 8th Army was surrounded. Unlike its two sister Alpini divisions it was unable to escape the pocket. By January 28, 1943 the division had walked 200 km, fought 20 battles and lost 80% of its personnel in termperatures that reached minus 30 to 40 degrees Celcius at night. That day the divisions remnants were attacked by Cossacks and it ceased to exist. Only about 1,600 stragglers reached German lines.<cr><cr><cr><cr><cr>Entry courtesy Chris Munson

rejected.source: The 7th Reserve Army was formed 28 May 1942 as part of the Stavka Reserve (RVGK). Within one month, this force had been redesignated the 62nd Army. From mid August 1942 until late January 1943, the 62nd Army, under the command of General Vasily Chuikov, fought in the Battle of Stalingrad. 62nd Army conducted an epic defense of the city against repeated and desperate attacks by the German 6th Army. The Army, along with the 64th Army, was operating under the Soviet Stalingrad Front. After the German assault at Stalingrad had come to utter disaster, the 62nd Army was uniquely awarded the .<cr>On 1 November 1942 during the height of the Battle of Stalingrad, the 62nd Army commanded the 13th, 37th, and 39th Guards Rifle Divisions, the 45th, 95th, 112th, 138th, 193rd, 284th and 308th Rifle Divisions, the 42nd, 92nd, 115th, 124th, 149th, and 160th Rifle Brigades, the 84th Tank and 2nd Motor Rifle Brigades, the 115th Fortified Region, and 20 regiments of howitzer, gun, antitank, mortar, rocket, and anti-aircraft artillery among other support units. Many of these formations were burnt-out shells by the end of the Battle of Stalingrad, with many formations reduced to less than 5% of its original manpower. On 16 April 1943, the 62nd Army became the 8th Guards Army.<cr><cr>
rejected.translation: 第7预备集团军于1942年5月28日作为最高统帅部预备队（RVGK）的一部分组建。一个月后，该部队被重新指定为第62集团军。从1942年8月中旬到1943年1月底，第62集团军在瓦西里·丘伊科夫将军的指挥下，在斯大林格勒战役中作战。第62集团军进行了史诗般的防御战，抵御了德国第6集团军反复而绝望的攻击。该集团军与第64集团军一起隶属于苏联斯大林格勒方面军。<cr>在斯大林格勒战役最激烈的时候，即1942年11月1日，第62集团军指挥了第13、37和39近卫步兵师，第45、95、112、138、193、284和308步兵师，第42、92、115、124、149和160步兵旅，第84坦克旅和第2摩托化步兵旅，第115要塞区以及20个野战炮兵、加农炮、反坦克炮、迫击炮、火箭炮和防空炮团等支援单位。<cr>许多这些部队在斯大林格勒战役结束时已沦为残部，很多部队的人力减少到不足其原始人数的5%。1943年4月16日，第62集团军被改编为第8近卫集团军。

rejected.source: Originally numbered as the 10th Army, this combat unit was formed on 10 October 1939 with General Walther von Reichenau in command. Its primary mission was to guard the western defenses of Germany against British and French attacks during the Polish campaign. During the invasion of the Low Countries the 6th Army saw active service linking up with paratroopers and destroying fortifications at Eben-Emael, Lige, and Namur during the Battle of Belgium. The 6th Army was then involved in the breakthrough of the Paris defences on 12 June 1940, before acting as a northern flank for German forces along the Normandy coast during the closing stages of the Battle of France.<cr>The 6th Army began its involvement in the Russian Campaign as the spearhead of Army Group South. Shortly after being promoted to field marshal, von Reichenau died in an aircraft accident while being transported to a hospital after a heart attack in January 1942. He was succeeded by his former chief of staff, General der Panzertruppen Friedrich Paulus. Paulus led the 6th Army to a major victory at the Second Battle of Kharkov during the spring of 1942. This victory also sealed the 6th Army's destiny because it was selected by the Oberkommando des Heeres (OKH) for the attack on Stalingrad.<cr>On 28 June 1942, Army Group South began Fall Blau; the German Army's summer offensive into southern Russia. The goals of the operation were to secure both the oil fields at Baku, Azerbaijan, and the city of Stalingrad on the river Volga to protect the forces advancing into the Caucasus. After two months, the 6th Army reached the outskirts of Stalingrad on 23 August. On the same day, over 1,000 aircraft of the Luftwaffe Luftflotte 4 bombed the city, turning it into a massive inferno. Destroyed in a matter of hours, Stalingrad was now a charnel house; defended by the weak Soviet 62nd Army under the command of General Vasily Chuikov.<cr>Despite having the initiative, the 6th Army failed to obtain a quick victory. The Red Army put up determined resistance, taking the fight to the rubble-clogged city streets. Though having almost complete air superiority over Stalingrad, and with more artillery pieces than the Soviets, progress was reduced to no more than several meters a day. Soviet casualties in the ghastly urban fighting were horrendous, while German casualties were just as appalling. Eventually, by mid November, the 62nd Army had been pushed to the banks of the Volga; holding only three small landing zones along the riverfront. However, despite continued fighting, the 6th Army was unable to eliminate the remaining Soviet troops holding out in Stalingrad.<cr>On 19 November the Stavka launched Operaton Uranus, a massive attack by Soviet forces on the flanks of the German army. The first pincer attacked far to the west of the Don, with the second thrust beginning a day later attacking far to the south of Stalingrad. The 6th Army's flanks were protected by Romanian and Hungarian troops, who were ill-equipped to deal with such an attack. Very quickly, the Romanians and Hungarians were routed, and on 23 November, the pincers of the attack met at Kalach-na-Donu.<cr>The 6th Army was encircled, and a major relief operation, which quickly failed, was undertaken by Generalfeldmarschall Erich von Manstein on 12 December. After an additional month of fighting, the 6th Army was almost destroyed. Paulus was promoted by Hitler to the rank of Generalfeldmarschall on 31 January 1943, ostensibly in part because until that day no German field marshal had ever surrendered. In other words, Adolf Hitler expected Paulus to commit suicide, but Paulus soon surrendered to the Soviet forces, contrary to orders by The Fuhrer. The remaining forces of the 6th Army, under the independent command of General Karl Strecker, surrendered two days later in the Tractor Factory, just to the north of the prominent hill Mamaev Kurgan. Although this was not the definitive end of the 6th Army, the Battle of Stalingrad was one of the worst military disasters in German history. For the first time, an entire German field army had been destroyed and only 6,000 of over 100,000 soldiers of the 6th army that surrendered were to return to their homes.<cr>During the last days of the Stalingrad encirclement, Hitler, in denial of events, had one man from every division in the 6th Army flown out in order to 'reconstitute' a new 6th Army (A.O.K. 6). This new formation became active on 5 March 1943, and was commanded by General Karl-Adolf Hollidt and based on Army Detachment Hollidt. It later fought in Ukraine and Romania as part of Army Group South and Army Group South Ukraine. The army was again largely destroyed in a large encirclement during the Jassy-Kishinev Offensive, but this time the army HQ survived. The 6th Army was the only German army to be encircled and destroyed thrice (including the final capitulation).<cr>In October 1944, under the command of General der Artillerie Maximilian Fretter-Pico, the 6th Army encircled and destroyed three Soviet tank corps of Mobile Group Pliyev under the command of Issa Pliyev in the Battle of Debrecen. During this time, the 6th Army had the Hungarian Second Army placed under its command, and it was known as 'Army Group Fretter-Pico' (Armeegruppe Fretter-Pico).<cr>Command passed to General der Panzertruppen Hermann Balck in December 1944. In January 1945, one of the 6th Army's subordinate units, IX SS Mountain Corps, was encircled in Budapest. SS-Gruppenfhrer Herbert Otto Gille IV SS Panzer Corps was transferred to the 6th Army's command and a relief attempt, codenamed Operation Konrad, was launched during the 46-day-long Siege of Budapest.<cr>After the failure of Konrad III, the 6th Army was made part of 'Army Group Balck' (Armeegruppe Balck). This army group fell back to the area near Lake Balaton. Several units, including the III Panzer Corps, were involved in Operation Spring Awakening, while the rest of the Sixth Army provided defence for the left flank of the offensive, in the region west Szkesfehrvr. After the failure of the offensive, the Sixth Army held the line until a major Soviet offensive, the Vienna Offensive on 15 March 1945. This offensive tore a gap in the 6th Army between the IV SS Panzer Corps and the Third Hungarian Army (subordinated to Balck's command), shattering the formation.<cr>By the end of March 1945, the 6th Army was involved in a retreat towards Vienna. The shattered remnants of 6th Army surrendered to the Americans on 9 May 1945.<cr><cr>

最初编为第10集团军，该战斗单位于1939年10月10日成立，由瓦尔特·冯·里宾特洛甫上将指挥。其主要任务是在波兰战役期间保卫德国西部防线免受英法联军的攻击。在入侵低地国家时，第6集团军投入实战，与空降部队协同作战，在比利时战役中摧毁了埃本-埃马尔、列日和南锡等地的工事。1940年6月12日，第6集团军突破巴黎防线后，作为德军在诺曼底海岸北部翼侧参与法国战役后期阶段的行动。<cr>第6集团军开始介入俄国战役时是南方集团军群的尖刀部队。里宾特洛甫晋升为元帅不久，在1942年1月因心脏病发作被送往医院途中遭遇空难身亡。他由前参谋长弗里德里希·保卢斯接替指挥。保卢斯带领第6集团军在1942年春季的第二次哈尔科夫战役中取得重大胜利，这一胜利也决定了第6集团军的命运，因为它被陆军总司令部（OKH）选为进攻斯大林格勒的攻击部队。1942年6月28日，南方集团军群开始实施蓝色行动；这是德军在夏季向南俄发起的进攻。该行动的目标是占领阿塞拜疆巴库的油田以及伏尔加河畔的战略城市斯大林格勒，以保护进入高加索地区的部队。两个月后，第6集团军于8月23日抵达斯大林格勒外围。<cr>同一天，德国空军第4航空队派出超过1000架飞机轰炸了这座城市，将其变成一片火海。几小时内被摧毁的斯大林格勒现在成为一座屠场；由瓦西里·丘伊科夫将军指挥的虚弱苏联第62集团军负责防守。<cr>尽管拥有主动性，但第6集团军未能迅速取胜。红军进行了顽强抵抗，在满是废墟的城市街道上与德军激战。虽然几乎完全掌握制空权，并且炮兵数量超过苏军，但是每天的推进距离不超过几米。在惨烈的城市战斗中，苏联伤亡极其严重，而德国方面的损失同样惊人。<cr>最终到11月中旬，第62集团军被逼退至伏尔加河畔；仅控制着沿河岸线的三个小登陆区。然而尽管继续激战，第6集团军仍无法消灭坚守在斯大林格勒内的剩余苏军部队。11月19日，最高统帅部大本营发起了天王星行动，苏联军队对德军两翼发动了大规模攻击。第一个钳形攻势向顿河西进，第二个攻势则在一天后开始，从斯大林格勒以南发起进攻。第6集团军的侧翼由罗马尼亚和匈牙利部队保护，但这些部队装备不足，无法应对如此规模的攻击。很快，罗马尼亚和匈牙利军队被击溃，在11月23日，两个钳形攻势在卡拉萨-纳-顿河会合。<cr>第6集团军陷入包围圈中，德军元帅埃里希·冯·曼施坦因于12月12日发起了一次大规模救援行动，但很快失败。经过一个月的战斗后，第6集团军几乎被消灭。希特勒在1943年1月31日晋升保卢斯为德军元帅，部分原因是到那时为止还没有德国陆军元帅投降过。换句话说，阿道夫·希特勒希望保卢斯自杀，但保卢斯很快向苏军投降，违背了元首的命令。第6集团军剩余部队在独立指挥官卡尔·施泰克将军的带领下，在拖拉机厂内投降，该工厂位于著名的马梅耶夫高地以北。<cr>虽然这并不是第6集团军最终覆灭的确切时刻，但斯大林格勒战役是德国历史上最严重的军事灾难之一。这是第一次整个德军野战军团被摧毁，超过10万士兵中只有约6,000人得以返回家园。在斯大林格勒包围圈的最后几天，希特勒为了否认现实，从第6集团军中的每个师都派出一名军官飞离该地以“重组”新的第6集团军（A.O.K. 6）。这个新编成的部队于1943年3月5日开始活动，并由炮兵上将卡尔-阿道夫·霍利德特指挥，基地为霍利德特集群。后来它作为南方集团军群和南方乌克兰集团军群的一部分，在乌克兰和罗马尼亚作战。该集团军在雅西—奇西瑙攻势的大包围圈中再次被大量消灭，但这次司令部幸存下来。第6集团军是唯一三次被包围并摧毁的德军集团军（包括最终投降）。

1944年10月，在炮兵上将马克斯·弗雷特-皮科指挥下，第6集团军在德布勒森战役中包围并消灭了苏联移动部队普利耶夫下的三个坦克军。在此期间，第6集团军还被赋予指挥匈牙利第二集团军，并被称为“弗雷特-皮科集群”（Armeegruppe Fretter-Pico）。

1944年12月，指挥权移交给了装甲兵上将赫尔曼·巴克。1945年1月，第6集团军的一个下属单位——第IX山地党卫军军在布达佩斯被包围。第四党卫军装甲军由SS-集团将军赫伯特·奥托·吉勒指挥，并转交给第6集团军指挥，同时发起了代号为“康拉德行动”的解围尝试，在长达46天的布达佩斯围城战期间进行。在康拉德三世行动失败后，第6集团军被编入“南方集团军群”（巴尔克指挥的部队）。该集团军撤退到巴拉顿湖附近地区。包括III装甲军在内的多个单位参与了春季觉醒行动，而第6集团军其余部分则为进攻左翼提供防御，在塞克什费赫瓦尔以西地区作战。在进攻失败后，第6集团军坚守阵地直到1945年3月15日的维也纳攻势。这次攻势在第四党卫装甲军和第三匈牙利军（隶属于巴尔克指挥）之间撕开了一道缺口，将第6集团军击溃。<cr>到1945年3月底，第6集团军开始撤退至维也纳方向。被击溃的第6集团军残部于1945年5月9日向美军投降。

rejected.source: The 6th Mechanised Corps was formed on 15 July 1940 at Bialystok in the Western Special Military District. It was attached to the 10th Army in the Bialystok area and was under the command of Major General M.G. Khatskilevich when Operation Barbarossa began in June 1941.<cr> The 6th Mechanized Corps was heavily involved in the first battles with Germans. The tank divisions of 6th Mechanized Corps were inferior against the advancing German units often without infantry support and were relentlessly pounded by the German aircraft of the Luftflotte 2. Without adequate ammunition and with many tanks in a state of disrepair and sent to several different locations without fuel reserves, they were quickly immobilized.<cr>The only battle that 6th Mechanized Corps saw was an attack of 24 June, when it lost 2% of tanks. The corps dissipated soon without any other combat, with negligible losses to aircraft, and with distance traveled that hardly necessitated any fuel tanking or repairs. The corps dispersed on 27 June near Krynki, with the personnel retreating east in small groups, and the equipment being abandoned or destroyed en masse.<cr>The idea of mechanized corps were revived in the spring of 1942. The second formation of 6th Mechanized Corps was assembled in November 1942. On the basis of Headquarters' 14th Tank Corps, the 6th Mechanized Corps was reformed on Nov. 26, 1942 at the station Kostereva in accordance with NKO directive number 11905907ss and GABTU number 1105723 dated November 26, 1942. Major General of Armored Forces Semyon Ilyich Bogdanov was appointed the commander of the 6th Mechanized Corps.<cr>On December 18, 1942, 6th Mechanized Corps was assigned to the 2nd Guards Army of the Southern Front, where it was involved in stopping the onset of Operation Winter Storm. The Manstein's attempted breakthrough to the Sixth Army stationed in Stalingrad. On January 8, 1943, the Corps - participating in the counterattack - captured the Zimovniki station (Rostov Oblast), a vital point of the Luftwaffe's munitions supply chain. For this reason the Corps was given the honorific Zimovnikovsky. Soon it was raised to the elite 'Guards' status; thus it became the 5th Zimovnikovsky Guards Mechanised Corps.<cr><cr>
rejected.translation: 第六机械化军于1940年7月15日在比亚韦斯托克的西部特别军事区成立。它隶属于比亚韦斯托克地区的第十集团军，并在巴巴罗萨行动开始时由少将M.G.哈茨基列维奇指挥。<cr> 第六机械化军在与德军的第一批战斗中发挥了重要作用。第六机械化军的坦克师在面对没有步兵支援的推进中的德国部队时处于劣势，经常遭到空战第二航空队的无情轰炸。由于弹药不足且许多坦克因维修不当而分散到不同地点并且缺乏燃料储备，它们很快就被迫停止行动。<cr> 第六机械化军仅参与了6月24日的一次攻击，并损失了2%的坦克。该军在没有其他战斗的情况下迅速解散，飞机造成的损失微乎其微，行进距离也不需要大量加油或维修。该军于6月27日在克林基附近解散，人员向东分散撤退，装备被遗弃或大规模销毁。<cr> 机械化军的概念在1942年春天重新兴起。第六机械化军的第二次组建是在1942年11月进行的。根据司令部第十四坦克军的编制，第六机械化军于1942年11月26日在科斯特列瓦车站重组，并遵循了NKO指令编号11905907ss和GABTU编号1105723（日期均为1942年11月26日）。装甲部队少将谢苗·伊里奇·波格达诺夫被任命为第六机械化军的指挥官。<cr>1942年12月18日，第6机械化军被分配到南方方面军的第2近卫集团军，在那里参与阻止“冬季风暴”行动的攻势。曼施坦因试图突破驻扎在斯大林格勒的第6集团军防线。1943年1月8日，该军——参加反攻——占领了罗斯托夫州的齐莫夫尼基车站（德国空军弹药补给链上的关键点）。为此，该军获得了“齐莫夫尼基”的荣誉称号；不久后被提升为精英近卫部队；因此成为第5齐莫夫尼基近卫机械化军。<cr><cr>

rejected.source: The 7th Hungarian Infantry Brigade was formed in 1939. Its TOE consisted of 9,500 men under a major-general with 2 infantry regiments (each with 3 battalions and a machine gun company), an artillery regiment with 7 batteries and various support troops. In January 1942 the Germans demanded more Hungarian forces for the Eastern Front and most Hungarian infantry brigades were reclassified as 'light divisions'. Their TOE however remained largely unchanged. The brigade was renamed the 7th Light Division. The Hungarian Government reluctantly agreed to support the Germans 1942 summer offensive Fall Blau and allocated the Hungarian Second Army to the task. Each light division in the Second Army was reinforced with three battalions from sister divisions in Hungary but nonetheless each division was only slightly larger than half the size of its German counterparts. Second Army's role in the offensive was to guard the German northern flank on the Don River. During the Stalingrad Campaign the Second Army suffered over 60% casualties but was generally able to retreat in good order. As part of a general reorganization of the Hungarian Army after Stalingrad the 7th Light Division was merged with other units and renamed the 7th Infantry Division. The division was disbanded in August of 1944.<cr><cr>Dr. Nigel Thomas and Lazlo Pal Szabo, The Royal Hungarian Army in World War II<cr><cr>Entry courtesy Chris Munson
rejected.translation: 第7匈牙利步兵旅成立于1939年。其编制表包括9500人，由一名少将指挥，下辖2个步兵团（每个团有3个营和一个机枪连），一个炮兵团拥有7个炮兵连以及各种支援部队。1942年1月，德国要求匈牙利提供更多兵力参加东线作战，并且大多数匈牙利步兵旅被重新分类为“轻型师”。然而其编制表基本没有变化。该旅更名为第7轻型师。匈牙利政府勉强同意支持德军在1942年夏季的蓝色行动，将匈牙利第二集团军投入任务中。第二集团军中的每个轻型师都从匈牙利国内的兄弟部队得到3个营的增援，但即便如此，每个师仍然只有其德国同行的一半左右规模。第二集团军在进攻中的角色是保卫德军北线顿河沿岸的安全。在斯大林格勒战役期间，第二集团军伤亡超过60%% c，但仍能有组织地撤退。作为战后对匈牙利军队进行重组的一部分，第7轻型师与其他部队合并，并更名为第7步兵师。该师于1944年8月解散。<cr>参考文献：Dr. Nigel Thomas and Lazlo Pal Szabo, The Royal Hungarian Army in World War II<cr><cr>Entry courtesy Chris Munson<cr><cr>

rejected.source: The Italian Army in Russia (Armata Italiana in Russia, or ARMIR) was an army-sized unit of the Italian Royal Army (Regio Esercito Italiano) which fought on the Eastern Front during World War II. The ARMIR was also known as the 8th Italian Army and initially had 235,000 soldiers.<cr>In July 1942, the ARMIR was created when Italian dictator Benito Mussolini decided to scale up the Italian effort in the Soviet Union. The existing Italian Expeditionary Corps in Russia (Corpo di Spedizione Italiano in Russia, or CSIR) was expanded to become the ARMIR. Unlike the 'mobile' CSIR which it replaced, the ARMIR was primarily an infantry army. A good portion of the ARMIR was made up of mountain troops (Alpini). While in many ways the mountain troops added greatly to the capabilities of the ARMIR, in other ways these elite mountain fighters were ill-suited to the vast, flat expanses of southern Russia.<cr>Like the CSIR, the ARMIR included an Aviation Command (Comando Aereo) with a limited number of fighters, bombers, and transport aircraft. This command was part of the Regia Aeronautica (lit. 'Royal Air Force') and was also known as the Corpo Aereo Spedizione in Russia ('Air Expeditionary Corps in Russia').<cr>The ARMIR was subordinated to German Army Group B (Heeresgruppe B) commanded by General Maximilian von Weichs.<cr>Italian General Italo Gariboldi took command of the newly formed ARMIR from General Giovanni Messe. As commander of the CSIR, Messe had opposed an enlargement of the Italian contingent in Russia until it could be properly equipped. As a result, he was dismissed by Mussolini and the CSIR was expanded without his further input. Just prior to commanding the ARMIR, Gariboldi was the Governor-General of Italian Libya. He was criticized after the war for being too submissive to the Germans in North Africa.<cr>In late summer 1942, after participating in the conquest of eastern Ukraine, the highly-mobile riflemen (Bersaglieri) of the ARMIR eliminated the Soviet bridgehead at Serafimovi? on the Don river. Then, with the support of German tanks, the Gariboldi troops repelled a Soviet attack during the first defensive battle of the Don.<cr>Finally the ARMIR faced Operation Little Saturn in December 1942. The aim of this Soviet operation was the complete annihilation of the Italian 8th Army, as a result of the operations related to the Battle of Stalingrad.<cr>On December 11, 1942 the Soviet 63rd Army, backed by T-34 tanks and fighter-bombers, first attacked the weakest Italian sector. This sector was held on the right by the Ravenna and Cosseria infantry divisions. Indeed, from the Soviet bridgehead at Mamon, 15 divisionssupported by at least 100 tanksattacked the Italian Divisions, and although outnumbered 9 to 1, the Italians resisted until 19 December, when ARMIR headquarters finally ordered the battered divisions to withdraw. Only before Christmas both divisions were driven back and defeated, after heavy and bloody fighting.<cr>Meanwhile, on 17 December 1942, the Soviet 21st Army and the Soviet 5th Tank Army attacked and defeated what remained of the Romanians to the right of the Italians. At about the same time, the Soviet 3rd Tank Army and parts of the Soviet 40th Army hit the Hungarians to the left of the Italians. This resulted in a collapse of the Axis front, north of Stalingrad: the ARMIR was encircled, but for some days the Italian troops were ablewith huge casualtiesto stop the attacking Soviet troops.<cr>The Soviet 1st Guards Army then attacked the Italian center which was held by the 298th German, the Pasubio, the Torino, the Prince Amedeo Duca d'Aosta, and the Sforzesca divisions. After eleven days of bloody fighting against overwhelming Soviet forces, these divisions were surrounded and defeated and Russian air support resulted in the death of General Paolo Tarnassi, commander of the Italian armoured force in Russia.<cr>On 14 January 1943, after a short pause, the 6th Soviet Army attacked the Alpini divisions of the Italian Mountain Corps. These units had been placed on the left flank of the Italian army and, to date, were still relatively unaffected by the battle. However, the Alpinis position had turned critical after the collapse of the Italian center, the collapse of the Italian right flank, and the simultaneous collapse of the Hungarian troops to the left of the Alpini. The Julia Division and Cuneense Division were destroyed. Members of the 1st Alpini Regiment, part of Cuneese Division, burned the regimental flags to keep them from being captured. Part of the Tridentia Division and other withdrawing troops managed to escape the encirclement.<cr>On 26 January 1943, after heavy fighting which resulted in the Battle of Nikolayevka, the Alpini remnants breached the encirclement and reached new defensive positions set up to the west by the German Army (Wehrmacht Heer). But, by this time, the only operational fighting unit was the Tridentina Division and even it was not fully operational. The Tridentina Division had led the final breakout assault at Nikolajewka. Many of the troops who managed to escape were frostbitten, critically ill, and deeply demoralized: for practical purposes, the Italian Army in Russia did not exist anymore by February 1943.<cr>Mussolini disbanded what was left of the Italian 8th Army and the surviving Italian troops were unceremoniously brought home from Russia.<cr><cr>
rejected.translation: 意大利皇家陆军在俄罗斯部队（Armata Italiana in Russia，简称ARMIR）是意大利皇家陆军的一个军级单位，在第二次世界大战期间于东线作战。1942年7月，意大利独裁者贝尼托·墨索里尼决定扩大意大利在苏联的行动规模时，ARMIR成立，并将原有的意大利远征军俄罗斯部队（Corpo di Spedizione Italiano in Russia，简称CSIR）扩编为ARMIR。与被取代的“机动”CSIR不同，ARMIR主要是一支步兵部队，其中很大一部分是由山地部队（阿尔卑斯猎兵）组成的。虽然在很多方面，这些精英山地战士大大增强了ARMIR的能力，但在其他方面，他们并不适合俄罗斯南部广阔平坦的土地。<cr><cr>与CSIR一样，ARMIR也包括一个航空指挥部（Comando Aereo），拥有一定数量的战斗机、轰炸机和运输机。该指挥部隶属于意大利皇家空军（Regia Aeronautica），又称为空中远征军俄罗斯部队（Corpo Aereo Spedizione in Russia）。<cr><cr>ARMIR隶属于德军北方集团军群B（Heeresgruppe B），由马克斯米利安·冯·魏克斯将军指挥。<cr><cr><cr><cr>意大利将军伊塔洛·加里波尔迪接任了由乔瓦尼·梅塞将军新组建的ARMIR（意大利驻俄军队）指挥官职务。作为CSIR（意大利驻俄志愿军）的指挥官，梅塞反对在俄罗斯扩大意军规模，直到其能够得到充分装备。因此，墨索里尼解除了他的职务，并在没有他进一步参与的情况下扩充了CSIR。在担任ARMIR指挥官之前，加里波尔迪曾是意大利利比亚总督。战后他因在北非对德国过于顺从而受到批评。<cr>1942年夏末，在参加占领乌克兰东部的行动之后，ARMIR中的高机动步兵（掷弹兵）消灭了顿河畔塞拉芬诺沃的苏联桥头堡。随后，在德军坦克支援下，加里波尔迪部队击退了苏军在第一次顿河防御战中的进攻。<cr>1942年12月，ARMIR面临“小土星行动”。该行动旨在彻底消灭意大利第8集团军，这是与斯大林格勒战役相关的作战的一部分。<cr>1942年12月11日，得到T-34坦克和歼击机支援的苏联第63集团军首先攻击了最薄弱的意军防区。该防区由拉文纳步兵师和科塞里亚步兵师在右翼防守。事实上，从马蒙的苏军桥头堡出发，15个师得到至少100辆坦克支援，对意大利师发起进攻。尽管兵力对比为9:1，意军仍顽强抵抗至12月19日，ARMIR司令部最终下令疲惫不堪的部队撤离。<cr>圣诞节前，两支部队在激烈的战斗后被击溃并撤退。与此同时，1942年12月17日，苏联第21集团军和第5坦克集团军攻击并击败了意大利军队左侧的罗马尼亚残部。大约在同一时间，苏联第3装甲集团军和部分苏联第40集团军向意大利军队右侧的匈牙利部队发起了进攻。这导致轴心国在斯大林格勒以北的战线崩溃：ARMIR被包围，但数日内意军仍能以巨大的伤亡阻止苏军攻势。<cr>随后，苏联第1近卫集团军攻击了由德意志第298师、帕苏比奥师、都灵师、阿梅代奥亲王杜卡·达斯托亚师和索福塞卡师组成的意军中央阵地。经过十一天血腥的战斗，在压倒性的苏军攻势下，这些部队被包围并击败。苏联空军支援导致意大利装甲部队指挥官保罗·塔尔纳西将军阵亡。<cr>1943年1月14日，短暂休整后，第6苏联集团军攻击了意军山地师团的阿尔卑斯师。这些单位被部署在意军左翼，并且到目前为止相对未受战斗影响。然而，在意军中央战线崩溃、右翼战线崩溃以及同时左侧匈牙利部队崩溃之后，阿尔卑斯师的位置变得危急。朱莉娅师和昆内塞师被消灭。昆内塞师第1阿尔卑斯团成员烧毁了团旗以防止其落入敌手。特里迪齐亚师的部分和其他撤退部队设法逃出了包围圈。<cr>1943年1月26日，在尼古拉耶夫卡战役的激烈战斗之后，阿尔卑斯师残部突破了包围圈，并到达了德国陆军（国防军陆军）在西面设置的新防御阵地。然而，此时唯一能作战的部队只剩下特伦蒂纳师，而且它也未能完全投入战斗。特伦蒂纳师领导了尼古拉耶夫卡最后的突围突击。许多成功逃脱的士兵都患上了冻伤、严重疾病，并且士气低落：从实际意义上讲，意大利军队在俄罗斯已经不存在了。<cr>墨索里尼解散了意大利第8集团军剩余的部分，并将幸存的意军草草地撤回了意大利。<cr><cr>

rejected.source: The 9th Army first saw service along the Siegfried Line when it was involved in the Battle of France. It was kept as a strategic reserve and saw little fighting.<cr>By 1941, the Army was heavily strengthened and was deployed with Army Group Center for the invasion of the Soviet Union. In the initial phase of Operation Barbarossa the 9th Army formed the southern pincer of a massive encirclement of Soviet troops deployed at Bialystok with the German 4th Army forming the northern pincer. It continued its advance where it launched another pincer movement of Soviet troops at Smolensk. Even though successful in encircling Soviet troops, due to the large distances it had to cover, many Soviet troops escaped the pockets. Hitler then sent the Panzer forces from Army Group Center to the northern and southern fronts to inflict severe economic damage to the Soviet Union. The 9th Army remained static from late July 1941 until October 1941 when Hitler finally decided to launch his long awaited attack on Moscow.<cr>In front of Moscow were two elaborate defensive lines, the first was 250 km long in front of Vyazma and the second on Mozhaysk. The 9th Army struck from the north out flanking the Vyazma defensive line and along with the 3rd and 4th Panzer Armies, and encircling Soviet forces at Vyazma. This would prove to be the last major encirclement operation launched by the 9th Army.<cr>The 9th Army was placed on the northern flank as the German 2nd, 3rd and 4th Panzer and 4th Army would spearhead the offensive on Moscow. However the attack failed due to the cold weather, deteriorating supply situation and stubborn Soviet resistance. The Germans suffered severe losses in men and large parts of the 9th Army's troops were reallocated to the other depleted German Armies.<cr>The 9th Army remained in defensive positions in 1942, dug in 200 miles outside of Moscow as the Germans concentrated their offensive in Southern Russia. As the tide of the battle turned in Southern Russia, the Soviets launched Operation Mars, a major offensive against Army Group Center. The well dug in positions of Army Group Center defeated the Soviet offensive with heavy casualties.<cr>The Germans tried again in 1943 to regain the momentum in the Eastern Front by launching a massive pincer movement at the Kursk salient where 1/6th of all Soviet forces were deployed. The spearheads would be the German 9th Army and the 2nd Panzer Army from the north and the 4th Panzer Army along with Army Detachment Kempf from the south. The Soviets believed the heaviest blow would come from the north and massively reinforced the sector directly opposite 9th Army. By July 1943, the 9th Army had become the largest army ever fielded by the Germans even surpassing the much vaunted 6th Army with 335,000 men along with 600 tanks.<cr>Leading the advance from the north, the 9th Army ran into powerful Soviet defenses, and it gained no more than 10 km on the first day. Walter Model ordered the capture of the key and heavily fortified Ponyri railway station, which was needed to continue the advance towards Kursk. However, the Soviets had massively reinforced the town's defenses, which meant the attackers took very heavy losses. After a week of ferocious fighting, the 9th Army had gained just 20 km. After being unable to breach the enemy lines, the army was then forced to deal with the Soviet offensive which if not checked could have encircled the entire 9th Army. It fought a fighting withdrawal westwards throughout the remainder of 1943.<cr>By 1944, the 9th Army was exhausted, but it had received some badly needed reinforcements and was defending the area of Bobruysk in the first half of that year. On 22 June, the third anniversary of Operation Barbarossa, the Soviets began their colossal Operation Bagration whose overall objective was the destruction of Army Group Center. The 9th Army suffered nearly 80,000 casualties during Bagration of which 65,000 were taken prisoner. Nearly 40% of the 9th Army was destroyed in the summer of 1944. The army was then rebuilt by German units redeployed from Italy and was involved in the defence of Warsaw in autumn and winter of 1944.<cr>The Soviets began their invasion of Germany on January 12, 1945 and forced the 9th Army to retreat all along the front until it was deployed westward to the river Oder. Three of the 9th Army's formations were tasked with defending the Seelow Heights, which was the last defensible region before Berlin. To the north was the CI Army Corps, in the centre General Helmuth Weidling's LVI Panzer Corps, and to south of the Heights was the XI SS Panzer Corps. In addition south of Frankfurt (which was defended by the Frankfurt Garrison) was the V SS Mountain Corps. In total the 9th Army was reduced to 100,000 men and 800 tanks and assault guns against which the Soviets had over 1,000,000 men and 10,000 tanks and assault guns.<cr>The Battle of the Seelow Heights started on 16 April 1945 when Marshal Georgy Zhukov's 1st Belorussian Front attacked across the Oder. The 9th Army was able to hold the line for about 3 days. After very heavy fighting Weidling's LVI Panzer Corps was driven back towards Berlin. Most of the CI Army Corps divisions, now north of the salient created by the 1st Belorussian Front were reassigned along with LVI Panzer Corps to Army Detachment Steiner which was tasked with counter-attacking and pinching off the salient one of Hitler's impossible fantasies. In the end Weidling's corps was driven back into Berlin and he was promoted to commander of the Berlin Defensive Area, reporting directly to Hitler. Theodor Busse and the rest of the 9th Army were driven into a pocket in the Spree Forest south of the Seelow Heights and west of Frankfurt.<cr>From inside the pocket east of Frankfurt Busse organised a breakout to the west to join up with the 12th Army. The breakout, known as the Battle of Halbe proved to be very costly resulting in the destruction of the Ninth Army as a coherent force. Survivors that didn't surrender to the Soviets during the breakout crossed the Elbe at Tangermnde and surrendered to the US Army.<cr><cr>

第9集团军首次在西格弗里德防线服役，参与了法国战役。它被保留为战略预备队，并未参加太多战斗。<cr>到1941年，该集团军得到了加强，并部署于中央集团军群，准备入侵苏联。在巴巴罗萨行动初期阶段，第9集团军与德国第4集团军一起组成了对比亚斯特德克地区苏军的大包围圈的南翼钳形攻势。随后它继续推进，在斯摩棱斯克发起了另一场针对苏军的钳形攻势。<cr>尽管成功围困了部分苏军部队，但由于需要覆盖大片区域，许多苏军士兵得以逃脱包围圈。希特勒随后命令中央集团军群的装甲部队前往北方和南方前线，以对苏联造成严重的经济破坏。从1941年7月下旬到10月，第9集团军保持静态，直到希特勒最终决定发起他期待已久的莫斯科攻势。<cr>在莫斯科前方有两条复杂的防御线，第一条长250公里，在维亚兹马前，第二条则位于莫扎伊斯克。第9集团军从北面出击，绕过了维亚兹马防线，并与第3和第4装甲集团军一起包围了维亚兹马地区的苏军部队。<cr>这证明是第9集团军发起的最后一场大规模围困行动。<cr>在莫斯科攻势中，德国的第2、第3、第4装甲集团军以及第4集团军将作为进攻莫斯科的主力。然而由于严寒天气、补给恶化和苏联顽强抵抗，攻击最终失败了。德军遭受严重损失，第9集团军的大批部队被重新分配到其他兵力不足的德国集团军。<cr>第9集团军在1942年继续坚守莫斯科外围200英里处的防御阵地，当时德军将主要攻势集中在南俄地区。随着战局在南俄地区的转变，苏联发起了火星行动，对中央集团军群发动大规模进攻。然而，由于中央集团军群坚固的防御工事，苏军遭受了重大伤亡并未能成功。

1943年，德国试图通过库尔斯克突出部的大规模钳形攻势重新掌握东线战场的主动权。北部由第9装甲集团军和第2装甲集团军发起攻击，南部则有第4装甲集团军及坎普夫集群参与行动。苏联认为最猛烈的一击将来自北方，并在直接面对第9装甲集团军的地区进行了大规模增援。

到1943年7月，第9装甲集团军成为德军历史上规模最大的部队之一，拥有超过33.5万名士兵和600辆坦克，甚至超过了声名显赫的第6集团军。

作为北部攻势的先锋，第9装甲集团军遭遇了强大的苏联防御工事，在第一天仅推进了10公里。瓦尔特·莫德尔命令夺取关键且坚固设防的波尼里火车站，这是继续向库尔斯克推进所必需的关键节点。然而，由于苏军对城镇进行了大规模增援，攻击者遭受了重大伤亡。

经过一周激烈的战斗后，第9装甲集团军仅前进了20公里。在无法突破敌方防线的情况下，该部队被迫应对苏联的反攻，如果不加以阻止，可能会导致整个第9装甲集团军被包围。从1943年余下的时间里，它一直在进行艰苦的撤退行动。到1944年，第9集团军已经精疲力竭，但得到了一些急需的增援，并在当年上半年防御鲍里斯拉夫地区。6月22日，巴巴罗萨行动三周年纪念日，苏联开始执行庞大的巴格拉季昂行动，其总体目标是消灭中央集团军群。第9集团军在巴格拉季昂行动中伤亡近8万人，其中6.5万人被俘。1944年夏天，第9集团军几乎有40%的兵力被消灭。随后该集团军由从意大利重新部署来的德国部队重建，并参与了华沙秋季和冬季的防御战。<cr><cr>1945年1月12日，苏联开始入侵德国，迫使第9集团军全线撤退，直到部署到奥得河西岸为止。第9集团军的三个编制负责防守塞洛高地，这是柏林之前的最后一片可防御地区。北部是CI军，中部为赫尔穆特·魏德林将军指挥的LVI装甲军，南部则是XI党卫军装甲军。<cr>此外，在法兰克福以南（由法兰克福守备部队防守）的是V党卫军山地军。总体而言，第9集团军被削减至10万人和800辆坦克及突击炮，而苏联则拥有超过100万兵力和1万辆坦克及突击炮。<cr>1945年4月16日，朱可夫元帅指挥的第1白俄罗斯方面军开始进攻奥德河对岸的塞洛高地。第9集团军坚守了大约3天。经过激烈战斗，魏丁利指挥的LVI装甲军被迫撤退至柏林。大部分CI军区师团和LVI装甲军被重新分配给施泰纳集群，该集群的任务是反攻并封锁由第1白俄罗斯方面军创造的突出部——这是希特勒的一个不可能实现的梦想。最终，魏丁利的部队撤回了柏林，并被提升为柏林防御区域指挥官，直接向希特勒汇报。布塞和第9集团军其余部分则被迫退入施普雷森林南部、塞洛高地以南以及法兰克福西部的一个包围圈。<cr>在法兰克福东部的包围圈内，布塞组织了一次向西突围，试图与第12集团军会合。这次突围被称为哈尔贝之战，代价惨重，导致了第9集团军作为一个整体力量的毁灭。突围中幸存下来的部队没有向苏联投降，在坦格尔门德渡过易北河后向美军投降。<cr>

rejected.source: Army Group Center was the name of two distinct German strategic army groups that fought on the Eastern Front in World War II. The first Army Group Centre was created on 22 June 1941, as one of three German Army formations assigned to the invasion of the Soviet Union (Operation Barbarossa).<cr>On 22 June 1941, Nazi Germany and its Axis allies launched their surprise offensive into the Soviet Union. Their armies, totaling over three million men, were to advance in three geographical directions. Army Group Centre's initial strategic goal was to defeat the Soviet armies in Belarus and occupy Smolensk. To accomplish this, the army group planned for a rapid advance using Blitzkrieg operational methods for which purpose it commanded two panzer groups rather than one. A quick and decisive victory over the Soviet Union was expected by mid-November. The Army Group's other operational missions were to support the army groups on its northern and southern flanks, the army group boundary for the later being the Pripyat River.<cr>Army Group Centre was the strongest of the three German formations. Commanded by Field Marshal Fedor von Bock, it included the 4th and 9th Army, the 2nd and 3rd Panzer Groups and the 2nd Air Fleet. By mid-August 1941 it had crushed Soviet forces in huge encirclement battles: the Battle of Bialystok-Minsk and the Battle of Smolensk. In spite of terrible losses, Soviet resistance was fierce and self-sacrificing. A partisan movement disrupted German supply lines. Bitter fighting in the Battle of Smolensk as well as the Ltzen decision delayed the German advance for two months. The advance of Army Group Centre was further delayed as Hitler ordered a postponement of the offensive against Moscow in order to conquer Ukraine first.<cr>The German offensive against Moscow was resumed on 30 September 1941. The delay for the Ukraine campaign turned out to be fatal to the German forces fighting on the approaches to the Soviet capital. Autumn rains turned roads into mud. In November, an unusually harsh winter set in, catching the Germans ill-equipped for winter warfare. Meanwhile, Soviet resistance grew plainly desperate, as soldiers engaged in infantry combat against German tanks. Suffering tremendous losses, the Soviets finally stopped the German advance in late November 1941, when the advance elements of the Army Group Centre had the distant spires of the Moscow Kremlin in sight. The Soviet counter-offensive in the Battle of Moscow, which started on 6 December 1941, would mark the first decisive blow against the German invaders, and the failure of the German Blitzkrieg. Army Group Centre was driven back out of reach of Moscow by April 1942. It did however hold a narrow salient (the Rzhev Salient) which still threatened Moscow and would be the subject of numerous Soviet attacks in the coming year.<cr>1942 opened for Army Group Centre with continuing attacks from Soviet forces around Rzhev. The German Ninth Army was able to repel these attacks and stabilise its front, despite continuing large-scale partisan activity in its rear areas. Meanwhile the German strategic focus on the Eastern Front shifted to southwestern Russia, with the launching of Case Blue in June. This operation, aimed at the oilfields in the southwestern Caucasus, involved Army Group South alone, with the other German army groups giving up troops and equipment for the offensive. <cr>Despite the focus on the south, Army Group Centre continued to see fierce fighting throughout the year. While the Soviet attacks in early 1942 had not driven the Germans back, they had resulted in several Red Army units being trapped behind German lines. Eliminating the pockets took until July, the same month in which the Soviets made another attempt to break through the army group's front; the attempt failed, but the front line was pushed back closer to Rzhev. The largest Soviet operation in the army group's sector that year, Operation Mars, took place in November. It was launched concurrently with Operaton Uranus, the counteroffensive against the German assault on Stalingrad. The operation was repulsed with very heavy Soviet losses, although it did have the effect of pinning down German units that could have been sent to the fighting around Stalingrad.<cr>Following the disaster of Stalingrad and poor results of the Voronezh defensive operations, the army high command expected another attack on Army Group Centre in early 1943. However, Hitler had decided to strike first. Before this strike could be launched, Operation Bffel was launched to forestall any possible Soviet spring offensives, by evacuating the Rzhev Salient to shorten the frontline.<cr>In July and August 1943 the Soviets succeeded in stopping the German offensive Operaton Citadel into the Kursk Salient and counterattacked towards Orel and Kharkov. In tandem with the offensive into Ukraine another offensive, the Smolensk Operaton, was launched against Army Group Centre between August and October 1943. The attacks made slow progress but were successful in recapturing Smolensk and the important rail junction at Nevel, forcing the German line back on a broad front; however the attack foundered on the strong German defensive works in the Vitebsk-Orsha-Mogilev area (the Ostwall defensive line).<cr>Further Soviet offensives against Army Group Centre, the Gomel and Orsha Operations in November 1943 and the Vitebsk Operation in February 1944, were unsuccessful against the strong Ostwall defences. However, the Soviets did succeed in almost encircling the heavily fortified town of Vitebsk.<cr>In comparison to the great Soviet victories in Ukraine since Stalingrad, Soviet progress on the central front (roughly the area Minsk - Smolensk - Moscow) in the period early 1942 to early 1944 had been disappointing. Soviet planners launched several offensives hoping for a grand encirclement and destruction of Army Group Centre yet had only succeeded in forcing the German line back on a broad front with heavy Soviet casualties. There were several reasons for this comparative lack of success the terrain here was much more heavily forested and thus favoured the defender, German units in this area had had time to prepare comprehensive fortifications, and the German leadership had been better than the uninspired Soviet leadership.<cr>However, the defensive successes were to change in summer 1944. In the spring of that year, Stavka started concentrating massive forces along the front line in central Russia for a huge summer offensive against Army Group Centre. The Soviets also carried out a masterful deception campaign to convince the Germans that the main Soviet summer offensive would be launched further south, against Army Group North Ukraine. The German High Command was fooled and armored units were moved south out of Army Group Centre. The massive Soviet buildup opposite Army Group Centre was not detected.<cr>The offensive, code-named Operation Bagration, was launched on 22 June 1944, the third anniversary of the 1941 German invasion (this was actually a coincidence, the attack had been unexpectedly delayed several days). 185 Soviet divisions comprising 2.3 million soldiers and 4,000 tanks and assault guns smashed into the German positions on a front of 200 km. The 800,000-strong Army Group Centre was crushed. Up to 400,000 Germans became casualties. The Soviet forces raced forward, liberating Minsk on 3 July, the rest of Belorussia by mid-July, and reaching the Vistula and the Baltic States by early August. In terms of casualties this was the greatest German defeat of the entire war.<cr><cr>
